rootCause: The 200 is benign for the claimed privilege-escalation vector. The endpoint (setup.controller.ts:66-75, @Public) returns ONLY { tokenIssued: true } - it never returns the secret token in the HTTP body. The actual token is delivered exclusively to (a) container stdout/docker logs and (b) a root-readable mode-0600 file at /opt/deliverycentral-data/.setup-token (setup-token.service.ts:36-64). An unauthenticated network attacker therefore cannot recover the minted 256-bit random token and cannot pass SetupTokenGuard (setup-guard.ts:21-29, constant-time verify) on any destructive endpoint (/seed, /admin, /preflight/create-database, /migrations/apply). The admin Reset (/admin/setup/reset) is separately @RequireRoles('admin'), not token-gated, so it is unreachable regardless. There is no read-back path: /api/setup/status and /api/system/state expose only booleans/migration names, never the token. NOTE on why the 200 (not 400) occurs on seeded staging: at boot main.ts:145-171 only calls tokenService.issue() when setup.completedAt is null; on an installed deployment it is set, so the in-memory token stays null and isActive() returns false, so the controller's `if (isActive()) throw BadRequest` guard does not fire and a fresh token is minted. Residual (low-sev hardening only, NOT the claimed vector): issueToken() lacks the setup.completedAt check that getStatus() has, so an unauthenticated caller can arm a real SetupTokenGuard token post-install (idempotent, 24h TTL) and force log/host-file writes - harmless on its own, but it empowers anyone who already has log/file access and is log noise.
suggestedFix: Defense-in-depth: gate issueToken() on setup-incomplete state - in SetupController.issueToken() (setup.controller.ts:69) or SetupService.issueToken() (setup.service.ts:120), read platformSettings 'setup.completedAt' and throw BadRequest/404 when it is already set, mirroring getStatus() (setup.service.ts:96). This makes the endpoint a no-op once installed and removes the unauthenticated log/file-write side effect. Not security-critical since no secret is returned.
evidence: Guard logic: setup.controller.ts:70 `if (this.token.isActive()) throw new BadRequestException(...)` then setup.controller.ts:73-74 `await this.service.issueToken(); return { tokenIssued: true };` (NO secret returned). Token delivery channels are non-HTTP: setup-token.service.ts:46 logs token to stdout, setup-token.service.ts:54 writes mode-0600 file. Boot arming: main.ts:151 `needsSetup = !completed || completed.value === null;` and main.ts:162-164 only issue when needsSetup. SetupTokenGuard requires X-Setup-Token: setup-guard.ts:25. issueToken has no completedAt guard: setup.service.ts:120-122. Reset is admin-only: setup.controller.ts:237-238 (@RequireRoles('admin')). No token read-back: system.controller.ts:25-27 and setup.service.ts:92-117.
